automobila: automobil; gen. pl.: ima automobila — there are cars
bilo: biti — to be; bilo koji — any
da: conjunction: that, so that; da + verb = infinitive («da vidim» — to see); also «yes»
dan: noun masc.; dobar dan — good afternoon
dosta: adverb: quite a lot; dosta dobro — quite good
dođem: I will get there, I will arrive
doći; 1st pers. sg.: doći do — to get to
hvala: hvala vam puno — thank you very much
i: conjunction; before the word — «and, also, even»
izgleda: izgledati — to look; also parenthetical «apparently, seemingly»
išao: ići; past, masc.: ići na sigurno — to play it safe
je: biti — to be, 3rd pers. sg.; auxiliary verb past; je l' — «really, or what»
kod: preposition + gen. case: kod znaka — by the sign; kod Marija — at Mario's
koja: koji — which; fem.; also «which» (koja su to sela)
mi: mi — we; short form «me» (potreban mi je — I need)
mogao: moći — to be able; past, masc.
može: moći — to be able; 3rd pers. sg.; «može» — «all right, it's okay»
na: preposition: na jugu — in the south, na Instagram — in Instagram
nema: nemati — not to have; nema znaka — there is no sign
nije: negation of je: nije selo — this is not a village
prolazilo: prolaziti — to pass by; neut. past
puno: hvala puno — thank you very much
sad: = sada; e sad — well then, so
sam: biti, 1st pers. sg.: rekao sam — I said
stao: stati — to stop, to stand; past, masc.
ste: biti, 2nd pers. pl.: što ste tu — what are you doing here
u: preposition: + loc. case — where, + acc. case — where to
vas: short/full form acc. case of vi
za: preposition: za to — for this; skretanje za — turn onto
što: conjunction «what»; colloquial question «of what, why» (što si se sredio?)
